summary: Lassen NF lookout: 1913 ten-foot house, 1934 Aermotor cab on a 60-ft steel tower, lookouts and a 1914 eruption report; listed standing; public visiting rules not in sources.

facts.design: Aermotor 7x7 observation cab atop a 60-foot steel tower, plus a California Region 5 Plan BC-301 ground cabin (NHLR)
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Lassen National Forest

staffing.status: historically staffed (lookouts named in newspapers, 1914 to 1937); no current staffing stated

visit.trail_note: No source read says whether the public may visit or climb the tower today

events.note: Three 10-by-10 lookout houses built on the Lassen National Forest; one for Turner or Bald Mountain
Lookout counted seventeen balls of fire as Lassen Peak erupted, per 1914 newspapers; NHLR text prints the year as 1014
J.M. Stark was lookout; A.E. McDonnell had taken over by late September 1915
Supervisor began installing a summit water tank, to be filled with melting snow (October 1915)
The old water tank was crushed flat by heavy snow, found in summer 1922
Crew found a spring under the rock supplying about 20 gallons a day
Aermotor 7x7 observation cab on a 60-foot steel tower constructed
Lookout Oscar Edwall spotted smoke at 1:14 a.m. on July 3; Mineral crew called out and left within a minute
Tower remodeled and painted in August by the lookout and an ERA foreman (Lide Barber), with new windows; the Susanville paper gives its height as 65 feet
Photo caption dated July 3, 2002: calls one lookout the new and active one and labels another photo as the old tower

corrections.why: NHLR gives a 60-foot steel tower (about 18.3 m). The brief's 12.2 m is about 40 feet, and no source read gives that height. A 1937 newspaper gives 65 feet (about 19.8 m) after the remodel; the story notes the difference.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 60 feet for the steel tower. A 1937 newspaper, after the remodel, gives 65 feet. The record uses 18.3 m from the register and the story gives both figures.
NHLR's text prints the report as September 30, 1014. The 1914 newspapers quoted by Forest Lookouts date it to 1914, and the story uses 1914.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 12.2 is wrong; NHLR gives a 60-foot steel tower, so the record is corrected to 18.3 m, with the 1937 65-foot figure noted. Elevation 2103.1 m matches NHLR's 6,900 ft. The Forest Lookouts page has nothing after the August 1937 item, so the story is thin on 1938 to today; the 2002 photo captions are ambiguous about whether the lookout was replaced and no date is given. Access is unknown: no source read says whether the public may visit. Blog and trip-report pages found in search were not used. A further search for post-1937 Turner Mountain history (tower replacement, the 1913 house, current use) would be the next step. No photos added.
